name: Four Seasons Hotel Casa Medina Bogota
insider_take: This 1946 colonial masterpiece sits in the heart of Zona Rosa, where Spanish elegance meets modern luxury in Colombia's vibrant capital.
whats_special: The hotel occupies a meticulously restored Spanish colonial mansion that once served as a private residence for Bogotá's elite. Its stunning courtyard features original hand-painted tiles and a centuries-old fountain, while rooms showcase authentic period details like exposed wooden beams and wrought-iron balconies overlooking the bustling Zona Rosa district.
pro_tip: Request a room facing the interior courtyard for the most authentic colonial ambiance, and visit the rooftop terrace at sunset for breathtaking views of the Andean mountains surrounding Bogotá at 8,660 feet above sea level.
dont_miss: The hotel's prime location puts you steps away from the Gold Museum (world's largest collection of pre-Hispanic gold artifacts) and La Candelaria historic district. Book the hotel's exclusive emerald shopping tour – Colombia produces 70% of the world's finest emeralds, and their concierge has connections to the most reputable dealers.
pros: Historic boutique property with preserved colonial architecture
Prime location in upscale Zona Rosa neighborhood
Intimate luxury experience with personalized attention
cons: Smaller property size limits facilities compared to larger resorts
